narrative:
**Engagement jumped sharply across the board this week.** Model likes rose 74.5% to 10,300 across the 21,639 models tracked, space likes rose 44.0% to 779 across 6,081 spaces, and model downloads rose 17.8% to 2,689,045. All three engagement metrics moved together and by double digits, which is a larger one-week swing than the underlying inventory changes would suggest — worth confirming against next week's data before treating it as a durable level shift.

**Family mix rotated toward Llama and DeepSeek while Qwen thinned.** Llama-tagged models rose 72.5% to 1,848 (from roughly 1,071) and DeepSeek more than doubled, up 104.1% to 200. Qwen fell 17.6% to 5,156, Gemma fell 13.1% to 556, Mistral fell 13.2% to 99, and Nvidia-Nemotron fell 48.8% to 44; Kimi-Moonshot rose 61.9% to 34, though moves on bases in the tens should be read cautiously. Qwen nonetheless remained the largest identified family and led usage-side share, at 36.4% of 129 coding references (flat, -0.8%) and 27.2% of 507 chat-assistant references (+14.5%). The key methodology caveat: 8,210 of 21,639 models (37.9%) were unattributed as "unknown," so all family shares are computed on partial attribution, and the robotics family split was suppressed on a denominator of 8 — too few to report.

**On the Spaces side, growth concentrated in research and audio use cases.** Spaces coverage was complete (1.0) for the use-case cut. Scientific-tools spaces rose 17.5% to 208, search-research rose 16.2% to 351, music-generation rose 19.2% to 62, and voice-audio rose 11.1% to 361, while document-AI fell 7.6% to 387 and robotics fell 14.0% to 43. Chat-assistant remained the largest identified use case at 904 spaces (14.9% share). SDK distribution held steady, with static (3,343, +2.6%) and Gradio (2,106, +2.1%) together covering 89.6% of spaces. Technology penetration showed RAG up 20.8% to 2.70% and fine-tuned up 12.9% to 3.60%, against long-context down 21.6% to 0.26% — a base of roughly 16 spaces, so directionally weak evidence. By vertical, industrial-manufacturing rose 20.8% to 3.65% and healthcare rose 14.4% to 5.38%, while e-commerce/retail fell 7.9% to 4.11%. Next week, watch whether the Llama and DeepSeek model gains persist or reverse, and whether the outsized like growth holds at the new level.
